target_customer: Companies buying carbon removal credits (Shopify and Watershed reported as buyers)
problem: Direct air capture has very high upfront capital cost and long installation time.
business_model: Sell durable carbon removal credits and advance purchases; hardware deployed by the company

founders.name: Josh Santos
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him co-founder and chief carbon removal officer. Education from a search result about MIT startup coverage, not independently opened.

founders.name: Daniel Cavero
founders.background_notes: Roommates with Josh Santos when starting Noya per search coverage.

exit.reason: Co-founder Josh Santos announced on 2025-08-07 that the founders decided to wind down; reasons were not explained in the sources found. One analysis dates the closure September 2025.

competitors.name: Climeworks
competitors.traction_then: Orca plant in Iceland began operation 2021-09, 4,000 tons per year

technical_complexity.rationale: Direct air capture hardware and sorbent chemistry at modest capital cost; the cooling tower retrofit concept was later dropped because many towers move too little air.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary sorbent coated monolith and modular design, but well funded rivals and policy dependence.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it; Carbon Engineering was later acquired per one tracker, and Noya wound down in 2025.

market_need_then: Corporate demand for carbon removal credits was rising in 2021 and the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act raised DAC incentives, favoring projects with permanent storage and larger scale.

identity.voice_and_tone: Slogan: high quality carbon removal for this moment, all electric, interruptible, water positive

branding.brand_signature: Nautical metaphor: the company blog post titled Raising our sail to leverage DAC tailwinds (Josh Santos lists sailing as an interest on the YC page).

brand_strength.rationale: Known in climate circles with credible backers and press; no evidence the name drove growth.

pivots.from: Retrofitting existing cooling towers into CO2 capture
pivots.to: Modular direct air capture units with at least 1,000 tons per year per deployment
pivots.why: IRA incentive scale thresholds and low airflow of many cooling towers

outcome_analysis: Noya raised an 11 million dollar Series A in April 2023 from top climate investors and signed credit buyers like Shopify and Watershed, after pivoting from cooling tower retrofits to modular units when policy scale thresholds made the original idea unworkable. The founders announced a wind down in August 2025. They gave no detailed reason in the sources found, so the failure factors reflect commentary about the commercialization valley of death for DAC and the lack of a later round, which are inferences and flagged as such.
notes: Pre Series A funding is missing: MCJ Collective describes its seed investment and Dealroom lists a 125K YC entry in 2021-08 (single database, YC deal not recorded as a round). Seed size unknown; total raised unknown. Wind down date conflict (August announcement vs September closure). Competitor Climeworks source is dated about seven months after the batch. The noya.co site returned HTTP 503. Education of Santos not verified from an opened page.
